title: Rivergate and Current
premise: Astrid Ravensworth, a bush pilot dodging creditors and the memory of a grounded license, agrees to fly dying prospector Elias Crane out of the interior in exchange for a hand-drawn map to a lost river claim. But the map leads not to gold but to evidence that Rivergate Mining, the company bankrolling Astrid's debt, poisoned the water supply of an entire valley and buried the proof. Hunted by Rivergate's fixers and torn between the man who loves her and the law that would bury the truth with the valley, Astrid must choose between flying home safe and flying the evidence into daylight. In the end she crashes through a storm to deliver the documents to a federal hearing, losing her plane and nearly her life, but winning justice for the valley—and a new kind of freedom.
about_author: L. M. Vane is the pen name of a former northern bush-country writer who spent three seasons working remote airstrips before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose consciences cost more than their tickets home.

chapters.title: Fuel Debt
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Struggling to keep her de Havilland airborne and her debts hidden, Astrid takes a shady charter from Rivergate Mining to ferry supplies upriver. The beat establishes her desperation and pride: she'll fly anything except questions.

chapters.title: The Man in the Snow
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Forced down by weather at an abandoned camp, she finds prospector Elias Crane half-frozen and delirious, clutching a oilskin-wrapped map. He offers it for one promise: fly him out alive. The beat is wary compassion meeting opportunity.

chapters.title: A Promise Made at Altitude
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. With Crane bleeding out in the passenger seat, Astrid races a storm toward the settlement of Current. He whispers that the map shows where Rivergate hid its dead—not its gold. She lands; he dies on the dock. Beat: grief and dread.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knows
chapters.summary: Crane's widow Marta's POV. Marta reveals Elias spent his last season photographing poisoned creeks and dead game, convinced Rivergate was covering a spill. She gives Astrid his letters. Beat: reluctant inheritance of another person's war.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A Rivergate fixer named Corliss offers to buy 'anything Elias left' and makes clear refusal has consequences—her debt gets called within the hour. Beat: the trap closing, power flexing quietly.

chapters.title: The Co-Pilot
chapters.summary: Jonah Reyes's POV. Jonah, a bush mechanic who has loved Astrid for years, notices the map and offers to come along as navigator. Their banter masks fear; he knows what happened to the last pilot who crossed Rivergate. Beat: love offered without conditions.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Rivergate freezes her fuel accounts and files a complaint against her license. Stripped of legal ways to fly, Astrid realizes staying invisible means letting the valley stay poisoned. Beat: duty and conscience collide.

chapters.title: Night Fuel Run
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The pair siphon fuel and patch the old plane by lantern light while Corliss's men watch the airfield. A near-discovery forces them to hide together in the wheel well. Beat: intimacy forged in shared risk.

chapters.title: Up the Dead River
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Flying low through fog-choked canyons using only Crane's sketchy bearings, they find the first marker: a creek running orange, fish floating belly-up. Beat: awe curdling into horror—the map is true.

chapters.title: Camp Nine
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On foot, they locate the abandoned drill site where Crane worked: rusted drums, falsified logs, and a shallow grave pit of contaminated soil. Astrid photographs everything. Beat: evidence becomes burden.

chapters.title: The Valley That Remembers
chapters.summary: Marta's POV (interlude). Back in Current, Marta faces down Corliss alone, stalling him with a false trail so the expedition stays unfound. Beat: quiet courage; the fight isn't only in the bush.

chapters.title: Washed Out
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A flood destroys the landing strip; the plane is damaged and the radio drowned. Stranded with the evidence, they learn by shortwave that Rivergate has declared Crane's death an accident and blamed 'trespassing pilots.' Beat: isolation and fury.

chapters.title: Corliss Arrives
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. The fixer flies in with hired men, offering Astrid a fortune for the film and a warning about what happens to witnesses. His polished menace reveals the company's rot from inside. Beat: corruption made personal.

chapters.title: Smoke Signal
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Rather than surrender the photos, they burn their own camp as a decoy and scatter into the treeline, carrying the negatives sewn into Astrid's jacket. Beat: sacrifice of everything but the truth.

chapters.title: The Long Walk
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Days of pursuit through muskeg and rain; Jonah takes a fall protecting the film and fever sets in. Astrid must choose between speed and him. Beat: love tested against mission—she refuses to leave him.

chapters.title: Trapper's Mercy
chapters.summary: Shared POV. An old trapper, once paid off by Rivergate and ashamed of it, hides them and lends his canoe downstream. He tells them about a federal inspector arriving in Current within days. Beat: unexpected allies; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Running rapids at night with searchlights behind them, they capsize; the film case tears open. Astrid saves the negatives but loses the maps. Beat: desperate momentum, everything hanging by wet paper.

chapters.title: Current, Burning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They reach Current to find Corliss holding Marta and pressuring the town council. Astrid walks into the hall with the negatives in plain sight, daring him to shoot in front of everyone. Beat: confrontation—courage as spectacle.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Before the federal inspector, the photographs, Crane's letters, and the trapper's testimony land like hammer blows. Corliss produces a bribe; the town refuses it. Beat: justice outside the law finally entering it.

chapters.title: Last Flight
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Exposed, Corliss tries to destroy the evidence by torching the airfield hangar where the plane and negatives are stored. Astrid flies the burning bird out over the river. Beat: climax—everything risked at once.

chapters.title: Crash Landing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Smoke-filled cockpit, failing engine, Jonah shouting headings: Astrid puts the plane down hard on the river shallows, saving the film and each other, crawling out into the shallows as the wreck burns. Beat: survival, release, embrace.

chapters.title: Rivergate and Current
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. Months later: Rivergate collapses under indictment, the valley begins cleanup, and Astrid—license restored, debt dissolved—flies medicine runs again with Jonah beside her. She keeps Crane's compass on the dash. Beat: peace earned, love chosen over invisibility.
